newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian attorney says 2 women died in Detroit area.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian attorney says 2 women died in Detroit area.

text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian's attorney said Wednesday that two multiple sclerosis victims died in the Detroit area in the last 24 hours, but he refused to say whether the leading U.S. assisted suicide advocate was involved.

Lawyer Geoffrey Fieger made the statements at a hastily called news conference, at which Kevorkian was also present though he did not answer questions. The victims were women from New Jersey and California, Fieger said.

Fieger said he had been retained by both women. They died six days after Fieger said he had been retained by the family of a woman in Henderson, Nevada, whose body was found in a local hotel room June 26.

At the news conference, Kevorkian called for a panel of non-medical "dedicated, compassionate, intelligent and very honest people" to develop guidelines for assisted suicide on which the public could vote.
The U.S. Supreme Court ruled last week that there is not a constitutional right to assisted suicide and states have the right to outlaw the practice.

Kevorkian, a 69-year-old retired pathologist, has publicly admitted being present at 45 deaths since 1990, and Fieger has hinted he has been involved in more. A judge in Ionia, Michigan, declared a mistrial last month in Kevorkian's fourth assisted suicide trial. He was acquitted in three previous trials involving five deaths.
